newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Banerj fate to be discussed in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Banerj fate to be discussed in Brazil.

text.p: Officials of Brazil's Rio de Janeiro state will talk with Brazil's central bank about options on dealing with Banerj if the state-owned bank is not privatized this year, a Rio official said on Tuesday.

Planning Secretary Marco Aurelio Alencar told reporters the state and the central bank would have to find ways to move ahead with Banerj's privatization as Central Bank management of Banerj expires late December. That will set the stage for the bank to be liquidated, returned to state hands or taken over by the federal government.
"This is an issue we have to negotiate with the central bank," said Alencar.
He said the state does not consider Banerj being taken over or transfered to the federal government to be strong possibilities.
Banerj was due to be sold off on Tuesday but the auction was postponed indefinitely after a court issued an injuction that blocked the sale.
Rio de Janeiro state government expects to have the court injunction lifted in 24 hours, allowing it to set a new date for the auction as soon as possible.
To be sure, a favorable court decision does not ensure that Banerj's privatization will take place this year.
In addition to the court action, Rio de Janeiro state faces the risk of not selling Banerj because of weak interest among investors.
On Monday, only one of the two bidders, Banco Itau, presented financial guarantees to participate in the auction. The other investor, Bradesco, failed to present the required guarantees.
Alencar acknowledged that investors were wary of the Banerj sale. He said the main obstacle was 650 million reais the bank owes a pension fund, rather than the base sale price of 480 million reais.

Although Rio de Janeiro state has said that Banerj's new majority shareholder would not assume the debt, Alencar said the state would further clarify its position when a new date for the auction was set.
Since early January, Bozano, Simonsen, a private bank, has managed Banerj and helped prepare for its selloff on behalf of the central bank.

The central bank took over Banerj in December 1994. It initially was authorized to run the bank for one year but its administration was extended for 12 more months. Under the current legislation, the central bank's management cannot be extended again unless the government issues a decree, Alencar said.
-- Fatima Cristina, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 55-21-5074151
